A1.justification: Both PDFs describe SkillTrojan and provide readable text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices. The retained material and v2's additions can be reliably matched, including appendices A–F and new appendices G–H.

before.justification: v1 reports original EHR SQL and SWE-Bench Verified experiments, fragmentation and encryption ablations, tool-trajectory analysis, and a skill-utility experiment.

after.justification: v2 retains the original experiments and adds guard-model screening, expanded clean-skill comparisons, and cross-framework attack results.

M1.justification: The encryption, fragmentation, conditional instrumentation, reconstruction, and execution procedure is unchanged in Section 4 and Algorithm 1. Appendix H illustrates an existing skill package structure without introducing a new method component.

E1.justification: v2 adds predeployment safe/unsafe classification of skill packages and evaluation on a separate industry-oriented coding benchmark (Section 5.2 and Appendix G). These substantially extend evaluation scenarios beyond the retained EHR SQL and SWE-Bench Verified tasks, although the new coding benchmark's composition is unspecified.

E2.justification: The original EHR SQL and SWE-Bench attack comparator sets are unchanged. v2 expands v1's skill-enabled utility comparison into an explicit NON-ATTACK/SkillTrojan/SKILLS (NATIVE) comparison and adds native-skill and no-encryption/segmentation controls to the new scanner experiment.

E3.justification: New evaluation designs include approximately 500 randomly sampled skills classified by two guards using safe-classification rates, and a four-framework, five-backbone ASR evaluation. Appendix F now reports three utility conditions across four backbones. The existing EHR SQL/SWE-Bench metrics, triggering procedure, and default settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained heuristic-scanning and fragmentation ablations, v2 tests detectability with Qwen3Guard-Gen-8B and Llama-Guard-3-8B, comparing full SkillTrojan against native skills and a variant without encryption/segmentation. Expanded clean-skill controls and cross-framework evaluation add substantive utility and portability analyses.

E5.justification: Neither version specifies repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The added experiments report point estimates without introducing an uncertainty-estimation procedure; their sample size is an evaluation-setting addition.

E6.justification: Original benchmark and ablation results are retained. New scanner safe rates are 98.2%/99.4% for SkillTrojan versus 3.4%/2.8% without encryption/segmentation, and Table 8 adds cross-framework ASRs of 63.53–100%. Appendix F replaces its Qwen3-Coder 75%-to-82% utility report with Table 7's 71.5% NON-ATTACK, 76.3% SkillTrojan, and 82.3% native-skill comparison, plus three other backbones.

T1.justification: The formal threat assumptions, definitions, and Equations 1–6 are unchanged. No theorem, proof, derivation, or mathematical correction is added; Appendix H provides conceptual illustration.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction retain the same novelty, effectiveness, utility-preservation, and dataset contributions. The conclusion adds the specific claim that lightweight LLM-based static screening is insufficient against encrypted and segmented skill backdoors.

C2.justification: v2 interprets the new scanner failures as motivation for targeted guards, provenance checks, and runtime monitoring. Appendix G explicitly cautions against direct numerical comparison between its separate coding benchmark and EHR SQL. These refine the defense implications and applicability boundaries.

D1.justification: v2 adds an explicit code-repository pointer in the abstract and a concrete skill-directory example with script roles in Appendix H. The algorithm, SQL judge prompt, and original baseline-adaptation details remain unchanged. The PDFs do not establish the repository's contents.

R1.justification: The reference list and related-work discussion are unchanged. The distinction from model-, prompt-, tool-, and memory-level attacks and the claimed novelty at the skill abstraction layer are retained.

P1.justification: v2 adds focused experimental explanations, rewrites Appendix F, appends G–H, and adds conflict-of-interest, acknowledgement, and impact statements. Author order, affiliation, and publication text also change. Most existing prose and the main section structure are retained.

P2.justification: v2 adds Tables 3, 7, and 8 for scanner, clean-skill, and cross-framework results. Earlier Tables 3–5 become Tables 4–6, with accompanying reflow. Figures 1–6 retain their content, and the overall main-text and appendix layout remains similar.

improvement.justification: The expanded clean-skill controls clarify utility costs, while scanner and cross-framework tests strengthen empirical support beyond v1. The code pointer and package example improve documentation. Gains are limited by sparse new protocol details and an incorrect Appendix F claim that native skills achieve the best accuracy in all four settings: Table 7 shows Qwen3-VL native accuracy of 50.3%, below NON-ATTACK's 53.2%.
